title: Boeuf Bourguignon
subtitle: Burgundian beef braised in red wine
excerpt: The great French beef braise: chunks of beef shoulder slow-cooked for three hours in Burgundy wine with lardons, pearl onions, mushrooms, and a bouquet garni until the beef yields completely and the wine becomes a deep, velvety sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon is the definitive dish of Burgundy and one of the most celebrated braises in the French canon, described by Julia Child as 'certainly one of the most delicious beef dishes concocted by man.' The dish is essentially a peasant wine braise — inexpensive braising beef cooked in the local wine — elevated by Child and others into an internationally recognised classic. The key distinction from other beef stews is the use of a full bottle of wine (Burgundy Pinot Noir being traditional, though any robust red works), the separate preparation and cooking of the garnish (lardons, pearl onions, and mushrooms), and the final reduction of the sauce to a glossy consistency. As with most braises it is better made a day ahead, chilled, defatted, and reheated.

content.text: Brown the beef in batches without crowding the pan; crowding causes steaming rather than browning. Marinating the beef in the wine overnight is optional but deepens the flavour. Make the dish a day in advance: the fat solidifies on the surface of the cooled stew and lifts off easily, and the flavour improves overnight.

items.preparation: a full bottle of red Burgundy or other Pinot Noir

content.text: Brown the lardons in the oil until crispy. Remove. Brown the beef in batches until deeply coloured on all sides. Remove. Cook the carrot and chopped onion in the fat until softened. Add the garlic and tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes.

Return the beef and lardons. Pour in the wine and stock. Add the bay and thyme. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook in the oven at 150°C / fan 130°C / gas 2 for 2.5 to 3 hours until the beef is very tender.

Strain the sauce and reduce if necessary. Brown the pearl onions in butter until golden. Fry the mushrooms in butter until coloured. Return the beef to the sauce with the onions and mushrooms. Reheat and serve with mashed potato or egg noodles.
